clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard, within the year: June's anxiety rose as she wrote to her sister Edna every day and her functioning fell as she kept to her bed for weeks; Walter distanced himself from June and cut off from his brother Harlan over their father's land money; Glen began fighting at his new school; and by September, June joined the church choir and her anxiety eased. The period settles as the family adjusted to the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan, within the year: Walter drank heavily and he and Glen blamed each other over the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, and Nora began wetting the bed that spring; Ida's heart trouble was found; and by October, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning trees. The period settles as Walter shifted toward work and the family toward a new footing.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen's functioning fell as he sat in the truck for hours, and he and Marian fought over money at night; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight, and kept to her room distancing from her mother; Walter drank again after six years off it; and by June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team. The period settles as Glen took work driving a delivery truck and the family's balance shifted.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into your house in January 1990 after selling her farm, within the year: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, and you distanced from Hollis as he worked late and kept out of the rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; your eczema flared on both hands; and you and Hollis fought most nights. By August 1991, after Wilma took a flat in town in June, your eczema cleared over the summer. The period settles as the household adjusted to her absence.
